approval: Not approved. Owner requested original direct-write reuse analysis before considering extra error handling.
source_review: VrReadNamedPipe can report MORE_DATA as success; do not change ok or its success branch. demStoreExtendedError returns a Boolean without establishing LastError. readFailureExit classifies LastError after disposing the guest lease. Existing dwReadError is not consumed after failure classification and can carry the saved value.
counter_review: Keep original BROKEN_PIPE -> AX0/CF0 behavior only when that is the genuine read failure. Reusing dwReadError avoids a new local; removing bufferLeaseActive=FALSE in the terminal return block is safe because neither successor returns to lease disposal. Do not move error policy into generic guest-memory helpers.

reuse_review.original_registration: msinit.asm passes DS:CX = EXTERR_LOCUS to SVC_DEMSETDTALOCATION; original demgset.c stores GetVDMAddr(DS,CX) in pExtendedError. Original demRead writes locus, WORD error, action, class; pointer field is not modified.
reuse_review.current_registration: demgset.c stores numeric DS:CX in extended_error_location; demStoreExtendedError reads and commits sizeof(DEMEXTERR), including the untouched pointer field.
reuse_review.raw_pointer_boundary: Current selected sas.h maps NtGetPtrToLinAddrByte to c_GetLinAdd. sim32.c resolves one linear address, c_GetLinAdd resolves only its first byte and on failed paging translation returns c_GetPhyAdd(0). Reacquiring that pointer alone proves neither complete-span mapping nor write access; retaining it across guest mappings is not equivalent to current-VM access.
reuse_review.original_reuse_candidate: sas_store and sas_storew resolve current linear addresses through bios_write_byte/word. They retain physical RAM/device dispatch and may enter biosDoInst -> host_simulate on failed external translation. Investigate those original semantics instead of adding a second write implementation.
reuse_review.pending: Prove DEM call-context compatibility with BIOS fault/reentry, cross-page word handling, unchanged unrelated pointer bytes, and mapping changes. No SAS implementation or retained pointer restoration has been made.
reuse_review.error_preservation_correction: Release with commit=0 short-circuits the provider write; inspected chain reaches validation, free and memset, not a guest write callback. Actual LastError overwrite by this production path is not yet proved. Do not justify the two-line defensive addition using an artificial clobbering stub alone.

reuse_review.sas_contract_difference: c_sas_storew splits page-crossing writes into high-byte then low-byte operations. Missing mappings invoke biosDoInst/host_simulate in VM mode; protected mode without registered selectors returns without writing. A void SAS call is not equivalent to a checked all-span commit. No direct restoration has been authorized by test existence.

registered_object_review.registration: DOS initialization, msinit.asm:328-333 passes DS:CX for DOSDATA EXTERR_LOCUS; project-wide source search found this registration and original demRead as sole pExtendedError writer. Not an arbitrary application buffer.
registered_object_review.layout: const2.asm places locus, WORD error, action, class consecutively inside SWAP_START..Swap_Always, followed by untouched EXTERRPT. srvcall.asm GET_DOS_DATA exports this swap interval to clients.
registered_object_review.map_evidence: Retained NTDOS.MAP gives DOSDATA 0794, EXTERR_LOCUS offset0325 and EXTERRPT032A. This is historical link-layout evidence, not proof of a particular installed image relocation/mapping.
registered_object_review.correction: Generic first-byte/cross-page/translation-failure observations are not proof of a defect in this fixed registered object. Original stable-pointer contract must be traced through the actual DOS-data mapping/swap lifecycle.
registered_object_review.remaining_decisive_question: Does the registered DOSDATA backing stay at the same host address while supported guests execute DEM named-pipe reads, or does the current CCPU map it to a different backing? Need an actual supported-path mapping witness or source-proven remapping; do not presume remapping from PSP behavior or arbitrary page-table tests.
